quest.title: The Omnipresent God
quest.description: Before the Raiden Shogun's martial might, you sense that initiating Yae Miko's plan may not be as easy as you thought. It might be best to leave Tenshukaku and make further plans from there...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x925, Primogem x30, Mora x44000, Memory of Violet Flash x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Talk to the Raiden Shogun within the Plane of Euthymia
Talk to the Raiden Shogun within the Plane of Euthymia

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Indulge my curiosity. What is the reason that I find you standing here before me once again?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Do you hope your foolhardiness will shelter those people? Or... was it simply a means of seeking an audience with me?

choices.text: The Fatui have deceived the Raiden Shogun.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Oh? Surely you didn't rouse me from my state of eternal meditation only to tell me this?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: If so, then you underestimate me. I am quite well-informed about the Vision Hunt Decree.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know everything that's going on outside?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Not so. Only everything that pertains to eternity.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Vision Hunt Decree has my tacit approval.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Fatui's actions thus far do not constitute a threat to eternity, otherwise... they would have been purged long ago.

choices.text: But the Vision Hunt Decree is damaging.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Individual ambition is inherently incompatible with eternity.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: What you might not realize is that all too often... people have far more to lose by chasing their dreams.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Consider this — no one will lose their life on account of having their Vision taken away...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Rather, those who have lost their lives are the ones who insisted on pursuing their own aspirations, are they not?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Teppei...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Traveler, your existence is unique in my eyes.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: There seems to be limitless uncertainty in you. To put it another way, you are the furthest thing from eternity.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: So I won't insist that you comprehend the meaning of my actions. What matters is that I tread the path of eternity on my people's behalf.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This is your Plane of Euthymia...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It is created by your consciousness, yes?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: That's right. I'm surprised you understand it so well...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Anyway. You're looking for a chance to shake my will... aren't you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not here to debate your ideas.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm here to demolish them.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: So be it. Well then, you who would defy eternity... Time for you to enlighten me.

choices.text: It comes at a great cost to the people of Inazuma.
The Vision Hunt Decree should never have existed.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You've lost, Ei.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...Yes, I have.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Why can you not trust your people, and in the power of their ambitions?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: These ambitions have transcended space and time. They are something that no one can snuff out.

choices.text: When people move forward with all their might...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Is this the lesson you learned from your journey in Liyue?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: There are nations where humans cast their god aside and stride forward...?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So, are we to just abandon the notion of progress... for the sake of wishful thinking?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...You and I have both witnessed the great loss that progress can bring.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Eternity... eternity is the only way...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The Heavenly Principles... Irrelevant nonsense as far as I am concerned.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: When all's said and done, all you really want is to protect your beloved Inazuma, forever and ever. Isn't that right?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: That would be something of an oversimplification.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But is this nation worth existing for eternity?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Stripped of ambitions, stripped of the potential for change, it does nothing more than simply... exist. It is a hollow shell of a nation.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Huh. I wonder what loss would it really be to anyone if such a nation were destroyed?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Miko, retract your words.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Never-changing eternity is the promise I made to my people.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But what your people need from you is not your promises. They want your attention... your divine gaze.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...You mean Visions?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Humans have a lifespan of barely a hundred years. They cannot afford to bear any extra losses.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But I have experienced it all. That is why I have chosen to guide them along the correct path toward eternity.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But eternity is far too cruel a fate for you, Ei.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: For me?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Not only have you stopped paying attention to the world, but you have stopped paying attention to yourself.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It must have been terribly lonely here, all alone, for centuries on end.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But it is necessary...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You will miss much by refusing progress... You seek to prevent loss, but have you considered all you are losing by remaining here in stasis for all eternity?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You are obviously lonely, and yet for the sake of eternity you choose to stretch your loneliness out to infinity...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Tell me this. Why is the sky here that was once so dark glowing again? Why now?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: This is your Plane of Euthymia. It's your inner world.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So it can only mean... that you are happy to see me again. You have found the loneliness here unbearable for a long time now, haven't you?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I... have nothing to say to that.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe, oh, but I have so much to say to you. Let me tell you all that has happened over the last few centuries.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: How long will that take?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As a fox envoy, I have an excellent memory. I recall every detail of the last few centuries with perfect clarity.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So it will probably take me another few centuries to relay it to you.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Heh... hehe... Miko, I never thought I would have the chance to meet with you like this again.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: *sigh* Seeing you again is a change to eternity... and a very nice surprise.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, since you are willing to admit that, I suppose that means we can still be friends?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: What a childish conversation this is.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Anyway. Now that I have been defeated by you and your plan, I will honor your wish to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But with regards to eternity and the question of whether this nation should move forward, I need time to give it some thought.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, you are the one who's been acting like a child from the very beginning.

choices.text: They can surpass the gods' expectations.
And even take over the work of the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what did you guys do in the Raiden Shogun's Plane of Euthymia anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the Vision Hunt Decree abolished?

choices.text: It was all thanks to Yae Miko.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, gotcha... Paimon was super worried, y'know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So maybe the reason Yae Miko is looking for us now is 'cause she wants to thank us? Let's go find her.

choices.text: We conveyed the wishes of the people.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Oh, hey there, {NICKNAME}. Nice to see ya!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't expect to see you here at this hour, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well, Cyno's out of the country on a trip, so he got me to come and help his subordinates take care of a few things. I guess you could say I'm his temporary substitute.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The atmosphere around here's not too bad nowadays, so I don't mind sticking around once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You've probably got a lot going on yourself, I'll bet? Good luck with everything!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Setaria, you should take a break and have a bite to eat.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Setaria?

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Ah, thank you! Sorry, I was completely absorbed in what I was doing, I didn't even hear your voice...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's alright. I'm glad that you enjoy the work you're doing.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Sorry you've ended up having to babysit me... I'm sure you have far more important things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Well, Rahman's busy with the Eremites these days. But having me stand in as your bodyguard must be a welcome breath of fresh air for you?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's a change for me, too — my first time working as a bodyguard. I'm just treating it as a chance to get a taste of Dehya's line of work.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I tried telling Mahamatra Cyno that I can work unsupervised. Really, this ought to be the last of his worries...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: He said that educators willing to work in the desert are an extremely rare breed, so I need a bodyguard for protection at all times... I think he's being a little overprotective.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: But at the end of the day, that's why we know we can count on the General Mahamatra. He and I are of the same mind in this case, so I am very happy to protect you.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: While you're in Aaru Village, we're partners. We don't want to cause you any unnecessary pressure. So please, try to enjoy your time here.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Whoa, did you two see that? A bird with huuuge wings just flew by!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: If Master Tighnari was here, he'd be able to tell you its scientific name, species, and behaviors...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But as for me... all I can tell you is, it isn't a species we have in Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Oh? Then what kinds of birds do you have in Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Dusk Birds! They have the most beautiful, vibrant colors. The feathers on their chest are the color of ripe Sunsettias, and their wing-tips are the color of tender Mint leaves.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: They're not too skittish around people, and at my tree holl— I mean, this tree that I often go past, there's a Dusk Bird there that always looks at me like it understands what I'm saying.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I once picked up one of its feathers from the ground, and it felt really nice...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: You have keen observation skills, and a love for living things. You'd be better served directing your energies there rather than sighing and whining all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Ugh, Eula says things in the most awkward way possible sometimes... Just ignore the second half, Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, it's fine, I know what she means. She does have a point...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Are you hungry for fish? I see quite a few over there.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Sounds like someone's up for a fishing contest, huh? Fair warning, though, I won't lose!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Seriously...? Another competition? I thought we were supposed to be sightseeing. ...Uh, but still — wait for me!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So this is Stormterror's Lair...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...From which direction will Stormterror appear, I wonder?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Um, excuse me...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Who's there?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, sorry, I didn't mean to disturb you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I apologize as well. I acted on force of habit. You must be a local, yes? My name is Cyno, and I'm here sightseeing in Mondstadt. In truth, it is I who am disturbing you.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Um, might I ask if you're looking for something here?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm waiting for Stormterror to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: You even set up a Kamera...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. I hope to capture a good picture as reference material for an artist I know.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Ah... In that case, let me help keep watch too. From what I've heard, Stormterror's movements have some... regular schedule.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Roughly how often does it appear?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Uh, hold on. I'll have to check against our data first. Let me consult my notes...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Um... Mr. Cyno, Sir, are you going to stand there staring into the sky the entire time?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm quite strong. My neck can take it.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: No, no, I mean... You should sit down. I—I brought a blanket — here, you can borrow it!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll be alright.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Oh, um... okay, well...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: ...Weird. Now I'm staring up into the sky, too...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I've heard that Cecilias only grow in remote spots at high-altitude, and that you're unlikely to ever see one unless you go looking for it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Though they can be preserved for a long time as specimens, I can't take back the beauty they possess in the wild. It's a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Shall I ask Sucrose to develop a Cecilia variant with improved soil adaptability for you?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I should warn you, though, it may very well end up with a name like "Tetratanic Ananemo Cecilia," or perhaps "Epsilon-Series Cecilia, Variation 601, Sumeru Growth-Type."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Is this you attempting to tell a joke?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Unfortunately not. I'm being completely serious.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: In that case, I look forward to... well, whichever of those two it ends up being.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Back to our previous topic — if you wish to use antitoxic compounds from Calla Lilies in an antidote, then I have a few suggestions...

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I wonder who will have the honor of offering the Windblume to Lord Barbatos this year?

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm so envious. If only I could be the one.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: (If I had to pick a flower to give away, which one should I choose? Agh, what a dilemma...)

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: (Let me think of this a different way. If... If I want to find the flower that fits Master Diluc the most...)

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: (Gosh... Now all I can think about is Diluc...)

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Welcome to Mondstadt — make sure you don't miss out on the Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival has its origins in Old Mondstadt, and the legend of the Windblume carries still to this day.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Even now, most Mondstadters believe that the Windblume Festival is a festival for lovers and that they should express their love with the most extravagant sincerity during this time.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Of course, there are also the more traditional amongst the Mondstadters who think that the key purpose behind the Windblume Festival is to celebrate Mondstadt's liberation. For them, this festival is more suited toward remembrance than love.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: I believe that both these perspectives are fine. Everyone should get to choose the way they wish to celebrate.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: I hope that everyone can find their own joy during this Windblume Festival, including you! Happy Windblume Festival, friend!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh, Traveler. As you can see, the Windblume Festival's come around again.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Every festival, there are plenty of youngsters that like to go out and adventure in the wilds.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ah, what can I say. I'm old. I know what these kids are thinking better than they do.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: To me, the Windblume Festival represents the continuation of the rebelliousness passed down by the resisting heroes from the era of the Stormlord of the Tower.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But... I suppose I can't expect the younger generation to think like me, right? Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Well, if the youngsters can feel the charm of adventuring through the spirit of the festival, I suppose it's worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* Traveler, what kind of gift do you think moves people the most?

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Windblumes... I'm sure Barbara-sama has already seen plenty of those and won't be interested at all.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: A letter... I think Barbara-sama gets plenty of those as well, and the feedback from her fans is virtually the same.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: I need to get her something more unique, something more eye-catching...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Huh, you mean we need to be careful not to cause any trouble for Barbara-sama? Ah, right, thanks for the reminder. That's really important too.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Barbara-sama's work is essential. As fans, we should do our utmost not to disturb her!

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: Huh? I recognize this voice... Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: The Windblume festivities are in full swing! If you get time, do make sure to roam around. You'll find a very different Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: Even better, if there's someone important to you, you should spend the festival with them. That's where the Windblume spirit truly resides...

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival is a celebration of comfort and warmth. If possible, I wish I could spend this time with my beloved, Godwin...

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: I still don't know how he's getting on... May the winds protect him.

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: So, just what kind of flower was the Windblume from Old Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: Modern Mondstadters have every opinion in the world about Windblumes, but they all seem to lack the desire to seek out tangible proof.

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: It might be that the atmosphere of this festival is too leisurely. I'm seeing wandering couples play at being adventurers without properly understanding what a real adventure is.

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: Hmph, I'm not like them. As a true scholar, I want to discover the truth behind the question, and won't be deterred by anything else!

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Mr. Doolan often tells me that we should go to Cape Oath to have a look. What a curious idea. It's not as if there are ruins there or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: Angel's Share is a great place to bring a date!

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: There's no need to trek all the way up to Starsnatch Cliff, nor is there a point in climbing the heights of Cape Oath. All you need to do is walk into a tavern, order two drinks, and chat the day away with your companions!

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: Apple cider, cherry cider... and delicious Dandelion Wine. If you want it, the Angel's Share's got it.

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: This is, after all, an industry thriving beneath the gaze of our esteemed Master Diluc. All beverages are supplied straight from the Dawn Winery.

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: So, how about it? Want to come in?

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Greetings, the Knights of Favonius are at your service.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Blessings of the Anemo Archon upon you. On this romantic festival, I bid you and your companions joy and cheer.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Hi, is there something you wanted my help with?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: If it's not urgent, please pardon me for not keeping you company.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: I did have to slip out, after all. I want to get my wife something special.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: ...And some wine while I'm at it. Ah, how can you be a Mondstadter if you don't get to drink, especially on a holiday?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: As for what kind of gift I should get her... well, I suppose I'll figure it out on the way to buy some wine.

dialogues.speaker: Eury
dialogues.text: Hello, are you here to buy something as well? Huh, you aren't?

dialogues.speaker: Eury
dialogues.text: *sigh* I envy people like you who can show restraint when shopping...

dialogues.speaker: Eury
dialogues.text: Especially during a holiday with special sales and discounts everywhere. I even find the wine very tempting...

dialogues.speaker: Eury
dialogues.text: Ah, no. I must control myself. Resist, Eury! If I get any wine, why, it'll only end up being consumed by my alcoholic of a husband!

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Huh. Am I seeing things, or was that the General Mahamatra I just saw walking around Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: ...I must be seeing things. The General Mahamatra is always busy. How's he supposed to find the time to wander around Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Must be because I've been reading too much lately, triggering flashbacks to all the nerve-wracking research I had to do at the Akademiya...

dialogues.speaker: Brook
dialogues.text: Oh, did the wondrous fragrance of my cooked meat draw another? Hehehe.

dialogues.speaker: Brook
dialogues.text: You can really tell it's the holidays when the streets are full in this little town. Even outlanders have come to visit.

dialogues.speaker: Brook
dialogues.text: I thought he was here to ask for directions, but instead he surprised me when he inquired if I knew how to make any dishes using Philanemo Mushrooms.

dialogues.speaker: Brook
dialogues.text: Cooking with Philanemo Mushrooms... isn't impossible. But at most, they just accent the meat.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Hmm, instead of celebrating the festival in the city, you're out here in the wilderness adventuring...

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Are you, perchance, also searching for the Windblume?

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: As far as I'm aware, "Windblume" was possibly once a code word for people who wished to stay in contact and plot resistance in secret...

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: But with the changing of the times, the relational understanding between the people and the idea of the Windblume has also shifted.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: In this modern age of peace and freedom, beyond just the Mondstadters, the peoples of other nations might instill a new significance into the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: If such is the case then, the very meaning behind the Windblume itself will likely be varied in expression.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: "A flower that is not of this world"... Could that be referring to the real Windblume?

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm sorry, I was preoccupied with thinking about something.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: An adorable child bought a storybook from me, but I remember there being a rather strange riddle within its pages.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: It might've been something that someone just accidentally left behind. You don't need to pay any special heed to it.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: I'm being serious, there really are heart-shaped Sunsettias around Cape Oath...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Bea, your eyes must have been playing tricks on you. Sunsettias just don't grow into that shape. It's against the laws of nature.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: And even if they did exist, there's no way that they could be sweeter than the ones I'm already selling.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Well, why don't we just go over to Cape Oath to have a look? It won't take long...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: No. This has to do with my convictions! Using visual attraction to sell fruit is just a cheap trick. I would never do that.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: ...Oh come on, why won't you just get it already...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Sorry? What did you just say?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: *cough* Uh, nothing... Come on, just consider it for a second!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Even if she's a close friend, my resolve won't be shaken... *hic*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: *hic* Oh, it's you...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: That's right. I'm Quinn of Quinn's Fruits. My booth is at...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Fresh fruits only at... Quinn's Fruits...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Wait... Have we met before?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's she?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Bea?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Dunno what she's thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Ever since the Windblume Festival began, she's been bugging me about Cape Oath and heart-shaped Sunsettias...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Sunsettias of that kind just don't exist...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: You'd agree, right? *hic*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: *hic* A... Another!

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Well, by the looks of you, I'd say you're an adventurer! Not going to stock up on some new equipment during the Windblume Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you have for sale?

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Take your pick from this selection. All Master's own handiwork, so you won't find any second-rate items here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival and adventurers...

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: A lot of couples will choose to have dates at Cape Oath, but there are some brave adventurer couples who will venture near Stormterror's Lair.

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: That area is simply crawling with monsters, so many adventurers will come here to purchase new equipment...

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: ...After all, if you were to be beaten by monsters in that place, you wouldn't just lose face — you'd be putting your companion in danger, too...

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: So each time the Windblume Festival rolls around, we smiths run brisker business than usual, so I suppose we can be thankful for that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Take care, and make sure to enjoy the Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Welcome to Floral Whisper. Are you looking to get someone a bouquet? It's the Windblume Festival, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to buy some flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Certainly. We have a fine selection, whether you're looking to give a bouquet to someone or even do some gardening yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival is an ancient tradition of Mondstadt's. A day for freedom and romance.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: When we speak of Windblume Festival tradition, I suppose it's about giving the "Windblume" in your heart to the person who's the most important to you, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: As to what flower the Windblume actually is, everyone's got their own opinions.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Well, that's freedom for you, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry for bothering you.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: I hope you'll enjoy yourself during the Windblume festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Marla, the Windblume Festival is here, and yet, it holds no meaning for me...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Oh, Marvin, say not that!

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: We do not have your father's approval, but this time for lovers is ours also...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: No, what I mean is that as long as I am with you, every day may as well be the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: You're right, Marvin. Our love is like the dandelions that bloom on Cape Oath...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Marla, no... Our love should not be a thing so fragile...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: No, I mean to say that though the dandelions are scattered by the wild winds, their lives will not thusly end.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Dandelion Seeds will fly to distant places, take root, and sprout there... One day, they will cover the length and breadth of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Oh, my darling Marla...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Oh, Marvin! My love...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Since it's the Windblume Festival, would you like to come to The Cat's Tail and have a few drinks?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: I might even give you some flowers... Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival had a very solemn meaning once...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: But nowadays, many people believe that it's just a time when they send flowers to others and get their feelings across.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Oh? Have someone you'd like to send flowers to, do you? Let me guess... is it me, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: ...Haha, don't be so nervous. I was just joking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, thanks...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Aww, don't be shy.

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: #Hey there, {M#amigo}{F#amiga}! Are you here to listen to Six-Fingered José's latest composition?

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: Hehe, fear not. My creations do not disappoint.

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: When it comes to the Windblume Festival, other bards think of love songs. Madre mía, no sense of invention...

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: I, Six-Fingered José, on the other hand, am not constrained by convention. I wish to eulogize the heroic epics of ages past! The people must remember that this is a day for commemorating heroes and resisting tyrants!

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: Even if, ahem... I haven't quite finished the last part yet. But once it's complete, it will bring my audience running back!

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: This is the time of the Windblume Festival, the season when dandelions float about in the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: I've always been looking forward to a time when I might express my love for my destined one amid a sea of billowing dandelions...

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: But I never expected Miss Patchi to be too absorbed in her research to understand a thing I was saying...

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: Nothing could be more boring than spending such a romantic festival buried knee-deep in books and ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: Who knows how long it'll take for her to understand these deep yet nebulous feelings of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wonder how Glory is doing...

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: I wish I could return to Mondstadt to see her... But I can't. How can I let her know that her lover is a coward and a deserter?

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: The best I can do now is clear out monsters and do my part to protect Mondstadt... and her.

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: Laugh if you want. I'm... I'm a useless man.

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival... Hmph, it's that time of the year again, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: I had an epiphany when I got divorced, and it was like waking from a long dream: the Windblume Festival should never have been associated with love at all!

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: Hah, it must have been the scheme of some scheming city merchants. Wouldn't they love to package every festival as something for lovers?

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: ...People in love have no rational thought to speak of. A little flattery here and there and their wallets open wide.

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, I've come to my senses now. These festivals are absolutely meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: ...And if not for the Windblume Festival, would I even have met that man? Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Foxes really are too difficult to catch. Just how exactly did the elders manage it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the foxes...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Oh! As Springvale hunters, this is one of our customs.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Every Windblume Festival, young hunters like me go to Wolvendom to catch foxes.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: When we catch one, we place a wreath of flowers on its head and release it. It's a prayer for finding love in the year ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Of course, only eligible young hunters like myself participate. Hunters that have already tied the knot, like Draff for example, they're not allowed to take part.

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: *sigh* Not even close. Foxes are so hard to catch.

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: I didn't catch one last Windblume Festival either. In fact, I nearly injured myself. I remember swearing that this time would be different...

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: ...and yet, low and behold, I've been outfoxed again. All I caught were a couple of squirrels.

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: That said... I wonder if Miss Sucrose could use her bio-alchemy to change squirrels into foxes?

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: I bet she could, haha...

choices.text: So everyone that catches a fox will find love?

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: Uh... if you always participate, your chances will increase exponentially...

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: ...in that sense, you're bound to bump into the right person eventually...

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: ...ahem. Anyway, that's what Draff's always telling us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Alright, see you next time.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Why, if it isn't my underclassman, Cyno. What a pleasant surprise it is to see you in Mondstadt during the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Greetings, Lisa. Though I'm sure you've been aware of my presence in Mondstadt for some time already.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Oh dear, looks like you've seen right through me. But I was in no hurry. I knew we'd see each other sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. It's just as Professor Cyrus said — shared aspirations always have a way of bringing people into each other's orbit.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hehe, he always has such a poetic way of wording things. I suppose that's the one respect in which I've taken after him, while in your case...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Yes, it's his wit and eccentricities that have left their mark on you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm. I'm not sure that describes me very aptly these days, given that I'm now the General Mahamatra. Still, if we're going to talk about ways with words, I think my deadpan humor is far superior than our professor's.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Is that so? Strange, I heard that you're just Cyno the Adventurer when you're in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...You make a good point.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: What do you think of Mondstadt during this time of year? It's quite nice, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. It's very nice. I think I'm starting to understand your reasons for leaving the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hehe. I've always prided myself on making wise decisions, and that was certainly one of them.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If our professor had been as sensible as you, he would have had a much easier time in his working life. Being stubborn doesn't help anybody.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well, if even you feel comfortable criticizing him now that he's retired... it really goes to show how much he's changed.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Stubbornness is an all-too-common vice among scholars. I hope that never rubs off on you. I'm always happy to see you visit Mondstadt, and experience the feeling of freedom for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I heard the latest news about Collei, too. No doubt the traumas of her childhood will persist for a while to come, but I have to say, she appears to be doing quite better this time than on previous visits.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I suppose you're something of a mentor to her, aren't you? Now that I think about it, the two of you aren't so dissimilar. The power of Hermanubis once brought you great suffering.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's all in the past now. Besides, Professor thankfully didn't treat me like a test subject for the priest's power like the higher-ups had hoped, even though I was a desert-dweller.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Instead, he gave me the tools I needed to lead the life I have today. He adopted me, educated me, taught me how to fit into society... I am very grateful to him.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: You are very gifted, and sometimes that can become its own curse. But he has reason to be grateful to you, too — without you as his son-slash-student, he may never have changed his stubborn ways.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: As a fellow student of his, I couldn't be happier for the two of you. ...Ah, look at how quickly this developed from small talk to a deep and serious conversation. That's one thing I do miss about my Akademiya days.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: By virtue of being another of his students, you are as much a part of professor's family as I. It's perfectly natural for a daughter to inherit her father's conversation style.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: If you say so... I suppose that means I get to call you "baby brother" from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Um... I—I'd rather you didn't...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hahaha, yes, there's the baby brother I remember.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Am I... Am I dreaming? Miss Ying'er, you really came all the way to Mondstadt to see me...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Wh—Why were you willing to make the trip? I still can't believe it...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Hehe, why wouldn't I want to come see you, hmm? It's not like a quick trip from Liyue to Mondstadt is completely unheard-of or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Also, isn't it time for you to drop the "Miss," and just call me Ying'er?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ying'er...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ying'er... Heh, I... I think I still need some time to get used to calling you that...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Hehe, look at you, already so flustered. And we're just getting started!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: No no, I, uh... I... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I'm just overwhelmed with happiness. Thank you so, so much for coming to see me for Windblume...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You liked the card back from Cyno, right? I must admit, I also spent a good amount of effort coming up with the design.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: His request was quite interesting. He wanted a dragon, a cool pose, and a design that would stand out and awe his opponents.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Although the commission was for himself, he wanted the back to be flashy enough to draw the attention of the opposing player. Perhaps, there's something that can be said about how when it comes to Genius Invokation TCG, friendship is more important than competition.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: He also said that such an impressive card back should be shared with friends. Since he gave it to you, this must mean he considers you to be a close friend.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, and speaking of, to repay my efforts, he also gifted me the card back as well. Hmm... maybe I'll also give the game a try.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Collei! Sucrose! I brought some home-cooked food, why don't we enjoy it together?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Really? Sounds great!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I—I must point out a small issue about your cooking! You have a tendency to put a little too much flavoring in your dishes...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Ahahaha, sorry! I guess I've been a little heavy-handed with the seasonings lately...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Are you feeling stressed recently? Do you want to find someone to play cards with? It really helps with stress, I promise!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Oh, that sounds like a good idea. If I recall, both you and Sucrose are pretty good players, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, we are! We've been playing together, and we were actually talking about this just a few days ago...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Since you are already familiar... would you mind also showing me the rules sometime?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yeah, Collei seems to be a natural at the game... Maybe she's already the best player out of all of us!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh!? Me!?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: That's right, you've been all the talk at the tavern. "That little girl from Sumeru is really good at the game... If I can find the chance, I would love to test my skills against her."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Really!?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Isn't that great, Collei? You've become a TCG celebrity!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, I... I... Ehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mona, look! I found a four-leaf clover. It's so pretty; do you like it?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh? Is it for me? Thank you, Klee!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Um, could you also say something nice to Klee?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Oh, of course! Ahem. I've actually gotten really good at this! Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: O Miss Klee, our mighty Spark Knight, you are the flame of hope for all of Mondstadt, and the vessel for...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Huh? What's a vessel?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Oh no, Klee doesn't seem to really appreciate this kind of praise. Okay, then...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Klee, you're super adorable, and your hat and backpack are the cutest! Did your mom get them for you?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Yep! Mom said that she picked them out with Dodoco, and Dodoco really loves this backpack, too! Which is why Dodoco's always hanging from the side!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mom also said that someone else was also helping her pick out the gifts that day... Hmm, what was the name again...?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Ah, if Klee remembers correctly, people would call her... the old hag.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Wait, the old hag!? ...Huh, okay, now that you mention it, the old hag does have a fondness for picking out hats...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for your surveying tips! I had no idea that the Sumeru Forest Watchers would also have expertise in this area... You really do know just about everything!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's only natural that Forest Watchers and surveyors would have some similar skills. We're both constantly outdoors and on the move, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'm glad I could help.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: If I can find the chance, I'd love to pay a visit to Sumeru as well! I've heard that the terrain is quite complicated there, and it'd be a treat to see it for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, "complicated" is indeed one way to put it. Visitors often get lost when they visit Sumeru for the first time, and they have a tendency to pick all kinds of mushrooms and fruits in the rainforest without discretion.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Ah, we get a lot of people here picking Philanemo Mushrooms as well...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Actually, have you ever tried adding them to a recipe? They are quite bland by themselves, but perhaps, the taste can be improved if they're cooked together with other ingredients...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: I've never tried that myself... But now that you mention it, I do want to give it a try...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm quite curious, too. Would you like to pick some together later?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Well, what do you think? I trust you've enjoyed this year's Windblume Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I'm happy to see you find the time amidst your busy adventures to return to Mondstadt and celebrate the winds of freedom with us.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: And if you have a moment now, would you care to hear a new love poem I wrote this year?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahem! Allow me to recite it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: This world has never seen such vibrant color / it bestows upon everyone a brilliant hue

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: A shade more ethereal than white / yet more radiant still than gold / it eases into your eyes / and restores to light a solitary soul

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm... maybe a bit too somber? Maybe I should write another one on Sweet Flowers instead...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you have time for a duel?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I don't know how to play.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Huh, really... I suppose you've been too busy with other things to pick up the game?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'd suggest you visit The Cat's Tail. There's a teacher there who's quite proficient with introducing beginners to the game. You can learn the basics from her.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The sooner you learn, the sooner we can duel.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I quite like my new card back. It goes perfectly with my deck.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I take it that you've also received your card back? Want to use it to play a round?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's play Genius Invokation TCG!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need to familiarize myself more with the deck and the rules...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No problem. Just come find me again when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: A well-deserved victory.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You played well. Let's have a rematch in a few minutes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Try talking to Timaeus.)

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Hi there, are you also interested in alchemy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Leave them alone.)

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: What do you think? Care to have a game of Floral Chess?

choices.text: Tell me a bit more about Floral Chess.

response.speaker: Plauen
response.text: The adventurer who designed this game said that his inspiration came from the billowing petals and the wind that pursues them...

response.speaker: Plauen
response.text: And the game is meant to imitate the... romanticism of pursuing these flower petals...

response.speaker: Plauen
response.text: From a player's perspective, though, I'd say it's more like being chased around by some balloons with flower petals and paper strips stuffed in them...

response.speaker: Plauen
response.text: The experience isn't bad, don't get me wrong, but where's the romanticism...?

response.speaker: Plauen
response.text: Yeah, see you. If you wanna give this a try, just come over and give me a shout.

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: Is this game really that romantic? I don't feel it at all...

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: Or maybe I just utterly lack artistic talent... or something...

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: Would you like to play a song? As long as you do your best to keep up with the rhythm and beat, you'll be able to strum up a storm with ease.

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: Focus only on the wind around you and the lovely song you wish to play, and all your troubles will surely fade away.

choices.text: I'll give it a go now.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: No problem. The scores are over here and ready for your perusal.

choices.text: I've got something else to do right now...

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: Oh, that's fine... You're welcome back any time, though!

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: Ah, I hope this event will go smoothly this time too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you working on?

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: I'm preparing to welcome guests here. We've got all sorts of fun activities lined up for the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: But some of the events are being held outside the city due to the large areas needed, so without a guide to tell people where things are happening, some of them are going to miss out!

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: That's why I've been stationed here and put in charge of introducing the festival's activities to everyone.

choices.text: Well, tell me all about it.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: There are three events taking place during the festival: "Ballads of Breeze," "Floral Pursuit," and "Breezy Snapshots."

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: The activity I'm in charge of, specifically, is "Ballads of Breeze." The other two representatives should also be at their stations and making some final preparations.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: Everyone's pretty excited, so here's to the smooth running of this year's Windblume Festival.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: May you have a happy time as well!

choices.text: What activities have we got lined up?

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: The photo-taking is in your capable hands, Traveler!

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: If we can call this a job well done, Cyrus should be more inclined to approve our request to set up a Kamera Club.

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: And as long as we can set it up, we should be able to attract more Kamera enthusiasts and further refine the art of taking pictures!

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: Perhaps we might even be able to invite hobbyists from other nations...

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: W—Well, would you look at that? I'm getting rather ahead of myself, aren't I? Focus, man, focus — focus on the work at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: My Kamera's in pretty good shape.

dialogues.speaker: Fassben
dialogues.text: C'mon, Fassben, you can do this — think about the Kamera Club!
